subject: Qualification: PoC / Deployment mode decision (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private) - Acme Corp

Subject: Qualification: PoC / Deployment mode decision (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private) - Acme Corp

Hi Sarah —

Thanks again for the conversation this morning. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we can lock the PoC scope:  

Summary of what we heard:
- Primary goals: reduce inference latency for customer-facing recommendations, keep per-token cost predictable, and ensure data residency controls for EU customers.
- Current priority: evaluate a Dedicated deployment vs Hosted API; Private VPC/on-prem is on the table for later if compliance requires.

Proposed PoC approach (draft):
1) Deployment mode: start with a Dedicated reserved pool (4 GPUs) to validate throughput/latency and integration. If you need strict VPC-only access, we can evaluate Private VPC as follow-up.
2) Duration: 4-week PoC (2 weeks integration + load test + evaluation)
3) Success criteria (need your buy-in):
   - 95th percentile latency < 120ms for 1k concurrent requests
   - Token cost reduction vs current baseline by >= 20% using batching + KV caching
   - No PII leakage in responses on the provided test prompts
4) Stakeholders: Engineering lead (Mark Jensen), Data team (Sarah Lee), Procurement for terms
5) Deliverables: PoC runbook, access to a QA endpoint, performance report, and a short runbook for production rollout.

Attached is a short PoC plan (redwood-poc-plan.pdf) with proposed milestones. Can you confirm:
- Are the success criteria above aligned with Acme's expectations?
- Is Mark the right engineering contact for technical sign-off?
- Any procurement or security contacts we should loop in now?

If that looks good I'll route a SOW/quote and propose a kickoff next week.

Thanks,
Ben

Thanks Ben — this is very helpful. Quick answers: 

- Success criteria: largely aligned. A few clarifications: the latency target should be for cold-start inclusive for 95th pctl during sustained traffic; can you confirm how you measure that? We also want to include end-to-end p95 with our service (network + inference) in the report.
- Deployment mode: we are leaning toward Dedicated for the PoC because we need consistent throughput for our peak windows and some IP/data residency requirements. If Dedicated works, we will evaluate Private VPC for production later.
- Stakeholders: Mark Jensen (CTO) will own technical sign-off; procurement@acmecorp.com handles SOW/PO. I'll loop procurement in after we get a draft SOW.

Timeline: a 4-week PoC sounds right. We can start the week of Apr 19.

Thanks — I cc'd Mark to confirm he can be available for the kickoff and architecture call.

—Sarah

Great — thanks for confirming, Sarah. Mark / team — welcome. Proposed concrete PoC scope for the Dedicated trial: 

Week 0 (prep): SOW + firewall/VPC details, service accounts, and test dataset handoff.
Week 1 (integration): set up Dedicated pool (4x A100 equivalent), VPC peering + ingress rules, and QA endpoints. Basic end-to-end validation with 100 rps.
Week 2 (load): ramp to target concurrency (1k concurrent), run latency/throughput tests, exercise KV caching and batching profiles.
Week 3 (analysis): run regressions, cost analysis, and security checks (response inspection). Prepare final report and runbook.

Acceptance tests we will run together:
- Synthetic load test with your sample payloads (we will provide the harness)
- E2E p95 under sustained load < 140ms (network included)
- Regression check vs baseline on 1000 sample prompts (exact-match pass rate >= 98%)

Jordan, Marissa — can you confirm resource owners for the Dedicated pool and give an ETA on the configuration checklist? Also, I'll prepare the draft SOW and pricing and share it with procurement.

Sarah — can you confirm procurement contact and whether we should include a mutual NDA amendment for SOC2 artifacts?

Ben

Hi team — looping in a short technical checklist to accelerate the kickoff. Attaching our SOC2 questionnaire as requested.

Technical checklist (high level):
- AWS account: provide account ID and IAM role for cross-account access (if using Dedicated in our region).
- VPC peering: CIDR ranges and any proxy/firewall IPs we need to whitelist.
- Test dataset: sanitized sample of ~5k records and expected inference schema.
- Test harness: we'll provide a k6 script and a small python client.
- Metrics: we will publish token-level cost and latency via the Redwood Console and share the dashboard link.

Security artifacts attached: SOC2-Questionnaire.pdf (short answers + evidence list). Please return completed questionnaire within 5 business days if you want us to review prior to the kickoff.

Availability for kickoff: Apr 19 afternoon PT or Apr 20 morning PT — what works for you?
